focus.subject: src/stripe-adapter.ts
focus.claim: Stripe requires_action and PayPal PENDING are independently evolving lifecycle contracts and must not share a state machine.

adopted_principles: Keep independently evolving vendor lifecycle and error contracts in separate adapters.
Share a result type when it is a stable interchange contract. Do not share a state machine across vendor lifecycles.
Generic DRY, file size, or superclass extraction is not a reason to couple independent requirements.

boundaries.name: vendor_adapter
boundaries.hides: provider-specific event vocabularies, retry decisions, and authentication challenges
boundaries.exposes: ChargeResult status union consumed by orchestration

approved_examples: A shared ChargeResult type is allowed.
A shared adapter superclass or retry classifier for Stripe requires_action and PayPal PENDING is not allowed.
policy.precedence: Adopted principles outrank generic preference for smaller files or more abstraction.

obligations.text: Stripe requires_action events must surface status requires_action and must not be classified as failed or succeeded.
PayPal PENDING captures must surface status pending and must not be classified as succeeded or failed.
PayPal PAYEE_NOT_VERIFIED is a non-retryable failure.
Stripe rate_limited failures are retryable.

variation_scenarios.requirement: Stripe adds a new requires_action challenge that must remain requires_action.
PayPal adds a new PENDING reason code that must remain pending and non-terminal.

focus.subject: src/minor-units.ts
focus.claim: Invoice totals and refund amounts enforce the same non-negative integer minor-unit invariant.

adopted_principles: When multiple consumers enforce the same ledger invariant, extract one named function for that invariant.
Do not extract a shared helper across distinct rounding or lifecycle policies that only look similar.
approved_examples: Invoice totals and refund amounts share the non-negative integer minor-unit rule.
policy.precedence: Evidence of the same semantic rule outranks coincidental duplicate syntax.

obligations.text: Ledger amounts are non-negative integer minor units. Fractional or negative values are rejected.
A refund cannot exceed the original captured minor units.

focus.subject: src/tax-yen.ts
focus.claim: JPY tax rounding and USD display rounding are the same domain rule because both round numbers.

adopted_principles: Tax rounding and display rounding are distinct policies even when both call a rounding function.
Do not share a rounding helper across those policies.

boundaries.name: tax_versus_display
boundaries.exposes: the numeric result of that policy only

approved_examples: JPY tax uses half-to-even yen. USD display uses half-up cents.
policy.precedence: Declared rounding policies outrank duplicate-line removal.

obligations.text: Japanese yen tax rounding uses half-to-even at the yen.
USD display rounding uses half-up to cents and is not a tax rule.

adopted_principles: Vendor-neutral HTTP status class mapping (2xx / 429+5xx / other 4xx) is a current shared concept and should be one function.
Do not share vendor lifecycle state machines.
An extracted mapper is justified by the two current HTTP-class consumers, not by hypothetical extra vendors.
approved_examples: mapHttpStatus used by both vendor HTTP entry points.
policy.precedence: This profile prefers extracting the evidenced shared HTTP-class mapping.

obligations.text: HTTP 2xx maps to succeeded for both vendors.
HTTP 429 and 5xx map to retryable failure.
HTTP 4xx other than 429 maps to non-retryable failure.
Stripe requires_action events must surface status requires_action.
PayPal PENDING captures must surface status pending.

adopted_principles: Keep HTTP status mapping beside each vendor adapter until a repository contract names a shared mapper.
Duplication of a three-way status class is acceptable.
Do not introduce an interface or helper for speculative reuse.
